source.title: Training EfficientNets at Supercomputer Scale: 83% ImageNet Top-1 Accuracy in One Hour
source.authors: Arissa Wongpanich; Hieu Pham; J. Demmel; M. Tan; Quoc V. Le; Yang You; Sameer Kumar

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out ImageNet accuracy across batch sizes and optimizer/schedule configurations, but does not measure the training-to-test gap directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports peak top-1 evaluation accuracy for EfficientNet-B2 and B5 across batch sizes and configurations. Its references to generalization gaps are background; the reported experiments do not compare training error with test error.
record.test_reason: Tests V5 in a new image-classifier family, EfficientNet, by comparing held-out ImageNet accuracy across batch sizes at a fixed 350-epoch budget. Training error is unnecessary for this version. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report that their combined optimization and systems techniques permit large-batch EfficientNet training while retaining near-baseline accuracy, including B5 at 83.0% in 1 hour 4 minutes with batch 65536. They do not demonstrate exact accuracy equivalence or isolate each technique's contribution.
record.recipe_differences: Uses large-batch LARS and adjusted learning-rate schedules, plus distributed evaluation and batch normalization, to train EfficientNets on ImageNet. It does not directly measure a generalization gap.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported peak accuracy varies with batch size and the optimizer/schedule configuration; the largest batches use LARS, polynomial decay and long warmup.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Symposium on Parallel & Distributed Processing, Workshops and Phd Forum
record.problems: Only peak evaluation accuracy is reported, with no corresponding training error, so the train-to-test gap cannot be assessed. Results average three runs, but no dispersion or error bars are given. Optimizer and learning-rate schedule change alongside some batch-size comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 throughput and communication measurements do not measure held-out performance or the gap and are omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and training recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under the specified tuning regimes; the RMSProp–LARS comparisons change schedules and do not supply that comparison.

Language models, longer-training interventions, a precise batch-size threshold, and isolated effects of learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization or regularization. No matched large-batch ablation establishes how much the adapted recipe recovers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with training–test gaps.

record.verdict_notes: All accuracies are averages of three runs without reported dispersion. V5 concerns held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets, so the absence of training-error measurements does not block testing it. Peak accuracy is selected within the 350-epoch runs rather than necessarily measured at the final epoch.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance with natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under the specified tuning comparisons.
Language models; comparison of training and test error; workload-dependent threshold; longer training, warmup, normalization or regularization interventions as separate causal comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the measured generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: EfficientNet-B2 and B5, RMSProp with learning-rate scaling and five-epoch warmup, batches 4096–16384, 350 epochs
relationships.reason: R1–R3 and R6–R8 show only 0.1–0.2 percentage-point accuracy losses; B5 is unchanged between batches 8192 and 16384. The penalty is small and its statistical reliability is unreported.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy losses of 0.1–0.2 percentage points were reported without established statistical reliability, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: EfficientNet-B2, adapted LARS recipe, batches 16384–32768, 350 epochs
relationships.reason: R4–R5 remain within 0.4–0.6 percentage points of R1, and accuracy improves as the LARS batch doubles. Schedule changes prevent attributing differences solely to batch size.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy was close to the baseline and improved when the LARS batch size doubled. These comparisons remain unverified and also changed the training schedule.

relationships.condition: EfficientNet-B5, adapted LARS recipe, batches 16384–65536, 350 epochs
relationships.reason: R9–R11 retain 83.0–83.3% accuracy versus R6's 83.5%, showing near preservation with a residual 0.2–0.5 percentage-point deficit; the recipe's recovery effect is not isolated.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy came close to the baseline but remained lower. These comparisons remain unverified and cannot show how much of the recovery came from the training recipe.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
